info.title: XrmMockup.PermissionAnalyzer.Tool
info.description: CLI tool that works out which Dataverse privileges your code needs, by static analysis

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: XrmMockup Permission Analyzer - Work out which Dataverse privileges your code needs, by static analysis, and check them against security roles

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --solution
options.description: Solution (.sln or .slnx) or project (.csproj) to analyze. A project is analyzed with the projects it references. Default: XrmMockup:Permissions:Solution, else the single solution in the current directory

options.name: --metadata
options.description: XrmMockup metadata folder. Default: XrmMockup:Permissions:MetadataDirectory, else XrmMockup:Metadata:OutputDirectory, else ./Metadata next to the configuration when it exists

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Leave out projects matching this pattern, e.g. "*.Tests" or "tests/*". Repeatable; adds to XrmMockup:Permissions:ExcludeProjects

options.name: --plugin-solution
options.description: A solution or project with plugin code that the analyzed code fires but doesn't include. Used for plugin cascades only. Repeatable; adds to XrmMockup:Permissions:PluginSolutions

options.name: --config
options.description: Configuration file. appsettings.{DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT}.json in its folder and environment variables apply over it. Default: appsettings.json in the current directory, when it exists

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: text, json, markdown (for a pull request comment or job summary) or sarif (for code scanning) [default: text]

options.name: --output
options.description: Write the report to this file instead of standard output

options.name: --detail
options.description: How much of the text report to show: minimal shows only the privileges to change per role, compact adds the entry points that need them, normal shows what needs attention with its sources, detailed adds granted requirements and assumptions, full adds every source and call path. Text only; the other formats ignore it [default: minimal]

options.name: --table
options.description: Only report requirements on these tables. Comma-separated or repeatable

options.name: --privilege
options.description: Only report these privileges, such as Write or prvBulkDelete. Comma-separated or repeatable

options.name: --runs-as
options.description: Only report requirements of these identities: Caller, User, ApplicationUser, ImpersonatedCaller or System. Comma-separated or repeatable

options.name: --basis
options.description: Only report requirements with these bases: direct, execute-privilege, all-implementations, all-lookup-targets or filter-unknown. Comma-separated or repeatable

options.name: --plugin
options.description: Only analyze one plugin, or some of its steps: <type>[:<message>[:<stage>]], e.g. AccountPostPlugin:Update

options.name: --custom-api
options.description: Only analyze one custom API, by unique name

options.name: --function
options.description: Only analyze one Azure Function, by function name

options.name: --entry
options.description: Only analyze this method, e.g. Contoso.Sync.Importer.Run, as an entry point. Repeatable

options.name: --operation
options.description: Only analyze a user operation on a table and the plugin steps it fires: "<message> <table>", e.g. "Update account"

options.name: --attributes
options.description: The columns the --operation sets, which decide the Update steps filtered on columns it fires. Comma-separated or repeatable

options.name: --role
options.description: Security role of the caller and the application user, by name. Repeatable; roles combine. Replaces XrmMockup:Permissions:Principals

options.name: --caller-role
options.description: Security role of the user that app code acts for by setting CallerId, by name. Repeatable

options.name: --no-roles
options.description: Only list what the code needs, without checking it against the roles in XrmMockup:Permissions:Principals and Users [default: False]

options.name: --fail-on-missing
options.description: Exit with 1 when the roles don't grant a privilege the code needs, and with 2 when there are no roles to check against [default: False]

options.name: --strict
options.description: Fail like --fail-on-missing, and also on unresolved operations, identities without roles and privileges that can't be checked [default: False]
